text: ARES requires a human preference validation set of approximately 150 to 300 annotated datapoints to compute confidence intervals using prediction-powered inference [S4][S5][S6]. In contrast, RAGAS uses GPT-3.5 as its judge with few-shot prompts that are not targeted for each evaluation domain [S1][S3]. The sources do not specify the exact number of human annotations required for RAGAS, only noting that ARES is more data-efficient than standard sampled annotation methods [S2].
